close_reason: Shipped option (c) in commit: corrected rustdoc on both the IoFailure.kind field (lib.rs:108-130) and the io_error_kind_serde module (lib.rs:147-198) to disclose the two known costs of Debug-of-ErrorKind serialization (not a contractually stable identifier; unknown variants degrade to ErrorKind::Other). Also closes PKIX-tit4.27 (Display-vs-Debug doc mismatch) as a side-effect. Filed PKIX-tit4.28 (human) to track the architectural (a) hand-maintained u8 table vs (b) drop kind entirely vs (c) keep-current-with-honest-docs decision, since (a) and (b) would reverse PKIX-2l0v.1 D3 and want explicit human input. Workspace tests + clippy --all-features -D warnings + rustdoc -D warnings all clean.
description:
pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs:147-198: the serde helper for io::ErrorKind serializes via format!("{:?}", kind), claiming in the rustdoc that "upstream documents this as the canonical textual identifier."

That claim is not accurate. io::ErrorKind upstream is a plain `#[derive(Debug)]` enum; the Debug output happens to be the variant name today, but the stdlib does NOT contractually guarantee this format. Display is the human-readable form (e.g. "entity not found"); there is no stable textual identifier API on io::ErrorKind at all.

Scenarios where this becomes a real maintenance cost:
  1. A future Rust release renames or restructures a Debug derive (e.g. adds a struct-like wrapper). All existing serialized payloads break decoding silently — they fall through to the catch-all `_ => ErrorKind::Other` arm.
  2. A new ErrorKind variant ships (the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`). Producers on newer Rust emit "FilesystemQuotaExceeded"; consumers on older Rust silently decode this to ErrorKind::Other, losing the diagnostic. The serde_round_trip test `io_failure_unknown_kind_falls_back_to_other` even validates that this lossy degradation happens — it is described as "forward-compat insurance" but it is silent data loss for cache replay.
  3. The Debug-of-ErrorKind contract is exactly the brittle "depend on Display output for parsing" pattern this workspace otherwise avoids.

Maintenance consequence: when this breaks, it will break silently. There is no compile-time signal; cache hits with the new producer / old consumer combination silently round-trip wrong, and tests pass.

Fix options:
  a) Serialize as a u8 mapped from a hand-maintained match table; treat new variants as a maintenance task on each stdlib bump.
  b) Drop ErrorKind entirely from the wire form and keep only `message: String`. Callers needing programmatic recovery have a richer message; callers needing `kind` for branching can grep the message.
  c) Keep the current code but rewrite the rustdoc to disclose that this is a best-effort textual representation with documented lossy degradation, not a "canonical identifier".

Option (b) is the most honest pre-1.0 choice — it admits ErrorKind round-tripping is hard and refuses to ship a half-solution.
title: IoFailure serde wire form depends on undocumented stdlib Debug behavior of io::ErrorKind
